open_obligations: Note that Wu et al.'s decomposition is fixed, not chosen by H or a model.
Check that Wu et al. train with RL from human feedback, not only supervised distillation.
Check whether leaf tasks are evaluated by humans in place of H's composition step.
in.other_title: Task decomposition: tree of simpler subtasks that help a human supervise the parent
in.rationale: Christiano et al. instantiate amplification by delegation: H names subquestions, X answers them and H composes an answer. Wu et al. state their task decomposition follows Christiano et al. and others: a parent task splits into simpler subtasks whose responses help a human provide a training signal, and the model learns Decompose and Respond/Compose operations; in their book experiments the decomposition is fixed algorithmic chunking.
in.scope: proposed EXTENDS: task decomposition to supervise tasks humans cannot evaluate directly, applied to recursive book summarisation

text: The paper instantiates Amplify_H(X) by delegation: H identifies a sequence of subquestions, X computes a subanswer to each, and H decides how to answer the original question after seeing the subanswers. X is an autoregressive model trained by supervised learning to predict Amplify_H(X)'s output; the authors note future work could instead use imitation learning or use Amplify_H(X) to define a reward for RL.
title: Amplification by delegation to subquestions with supervised distillation
